**Assessment**
Kishida’s 2024 record is mostly **positive** on `5B.4`: the clearest evidence points to rule-setting through formal councils, labor-market and industrial-policy expertise, wage-led growth, and broad regional support. I found **little direct evidence** of cronyism, family favoritism, or anti-competitive rule-making. The main negatives are indirect: political survival pressure and a tougher migration regime that narrows participation rules for some outsiders.

1. **Policy Speech to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html | Kishida said the economy is the foundation of public finances, called for restoring wage-led growth, and said Japan should move steadily toward fiscal soundness through expenditure reform. This supports fair, predictable rules for investment and job creation rather than short-term patronage. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
2. **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html | Kishida approved budget guidelines based on medium- to long-term projections and framed policy around private-demand-led growth and wage increases above price rises. This is strong evidence of rule-based macro conditions favorable to entrepreneurship and investment. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
3. **Joint Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy and the Council of New Form of Capitalism Realization** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/21keizai.html | Kishida advanced the revised “New Form of Capitalism” package through formal councils, including broad subsidy measures and structural growth policy. This looks like institutional rule-making, not insider favoritism. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`, `5B.2`
4. **GX 2040 Leaders Panel** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 2, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html | Kishida brought business leaders and technical experts together with cabinet members to design long-horizon energy and industrial strategy. That is direct evidence of trying to shape competition and investment conditions through expert-led policymaking. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.1`
5. **Ministerial Council on Acceptance and Inclusion of Foreign Human Resources** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 9, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html | Kishida implemented an expert-panel report and told ministers to move forward with bills and labor-market reforms. This is evidence of using formal policy mechanisms to expand the labor supply and support job creation. | `5B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.1`
6. **Regional Revitalization Action** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html | Kishida said local communities need sustainable administrative services, digital tools, and grants. This supports broader geographic opportunity and a less Tokyo-centered economic playing field. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`, `4B.10`
7. **“Illegal foreigners zero” agenda** | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 page content | https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/ | The page defends tighter visa screening, deportation enforcement, and stricter refugee procedures. This is the clearest mixed/negative signal: it is administrative exclusionary control over migrants, which can narrow fair access to labor and entrepreneurship rules, though I found no evidence of broader cronyism. | `5B.4`, `4B.7`
8. **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362 | Reuters reported that the funding scandal pushed Kishida into defensive politics around popularity and the budget. This is indirect negative evidence that short-term survival pressures were affecting policy rule-setting. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`, `4B.10`
9. **Japan’s Kishida championed ‘new capitalism’ but was undone by yen** | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen | Reuters said Kishida pushed some of Japan’s biggest wage increases in decades, but weak purchasing power, the yen, and scandals blunted the payoff. This is mixed evidence: the pro-growth rules were real, but the environment remained fragile. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`

**Search Gap**
I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Kishida used economic rule-setting for rent extraction, family favoritism, or clear business-partner patronage. I also did not find a clean direct source on property-rights reform or trade-policy distortion in 2024; the available evidence is mostly about wage policy, structural reform, labor markets, regional revitalization, and investment conditions.
